text:
frank: quick sync  noticed a gap in delegation: when proxy can't map a caller to a project it issues org-scoped tokens. hit this in a canary run and it overprivileged a job.

emma: oof. that's the fallback we kept around but we said it should be opt-in. can you share the rule id?

frank: rule id `proxy-delegate-default`. Request looked like:
```
POST /v1/exec
Authorization: Bearer proxy-token
X-Requested-Project: proj-99
```
proxy matched `delegate:org-default` and minted `org:write`.

raj: that is bad for contractor/external workloads. we should flip default to deny and add an explicit allow flag per route.

emma: agree. plan: (a) deny-by-default behind feature-flag, (b) add `X-Allow-legacy-fallback: true` for migrations, (c) log requested vs granted scope and mapping id.

frank: also suggest whitelist: never allow fallback for untrusted principals (define untrusted = external, contractor, third-party).

raj: add metric `proxy.delegation.fallback.count` and alert if >0.1% per minute in prod. ops will want that.

emma: infra-bot: deploy note?

infra-bot: config-change requires canary rollout to infra-canary, 30m stable window, and manual approval for prod.

frank: i'll open a small PR: change default behavior (flagged), add header, logging fields `requested_scope`, `granted_scope`, `mapping_rule_id`, and metric. will include migration checklist.

emma: please include a remediation link in logs/console for teams to add mapping or rotate keys.

raj: one more: ensure proxy never mints org-scoped tokens when caller explicitly requested project scope in header unless mapping is verified. fail fast otherwise.

frank: noted. i'll post PR link here and tag owners. thanks.
